questions.question: A 40-year-old man from Southeast Asia presents with an erythematous plaque on his leg with associated numbness, treated with various oral antibiotics with no effect. He has no systemic symptoms of infection.
questions.question_raw: Q58. 40M from SE Asia with erythematous plaque on leg with associated numbness, treated with various oral antibiotics with no effect. No systemic symptoms of infection.

parts.text: One investigation to best confirm the diagnosis?
Other than direct patient care, what is one other issue you might address with the patient?

parts_raw.text: B) One investigation to best confirm diagnosis?
C) Other than direct patient care, what is one other issue that you might address with the patient?

questions.model_answer:
a) Leprosy (Hansen disease, Mycobacterium leprae) — a single erythematous plaque with sensory loss (anesthesia within the lesion) in a person from an endemic region, unresponsive to standard antibiotics, is a paucibacillary (tuberculoid/borderline-tuberculoid) presentation.
b) Full-thickness punch skin biopsy taken from the active margin of the lesion, sent for histopathology with Fite acid-fast staining (the stain of choice for M. leprae); NHDP can confirm M. leprae by PCR. Histopathology is most helpful for confirming the diagnosis and determining the Ridley-Jopling form.
c) Evaluation of household/close contacts — contacts should be assessed for signs and symptoms of leprosy, given the chronic close-contact respiratory transmission; case identification also provides opportunity for contact education and, where used, chemo/BCG prophylaxis.
d) WHO multidrug therapy for paucibacillary leprosy for 6 months: dapsone 100 mg daily, rifampicin 600 mg once monthly, and clofazimine (50 mg daily plus 300 mg once monthly). Screen for G6PD deficiency before dapsone. (US/NHDP regimen uses the same drugs with daily rifampicin for 12 months.)

cohort_answer.text: A) Leprosy. B) Skin biopsy and AFB staining (Fite stain) - gold standard. C) Home contacts - all household contacts should be evaluated for signs/symptoms of leprosy. D) WHO recommends rifampicin, dapsone, clofazimine for all leprosy patients: 6 months for PB leprosy, 12 months for MB leprosy. Dapsone 100mg PO daily, Rifampin 600mg PO monthly, Clofazimine 300mg once monthly and 50mg PO daily.
